task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 implement Q-1053 / GH #2399 (local record docs/issues/ISS-1062.yaml) as ELIXIR-DEV (.claude/agents/elixir-dev.md; scripts/test_parallel.sh and test/scripts/ are in scope). The design is in handoffs/WF03-ISS1053SHARDFLAKE-20261012/step-01-issue-fixer.json (root causes RC-A..RC-D, fixes S1..S3, new tests, capture, stress protocol, mutants). The CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR returned FAIL with 4 MAJOR + 4 MINOR mechanical corrections in handoffs/WF03-ISS1053SHARDFLAKE-20261012/step-02b-code-design-validator.json (read its result, especially findings F1..F8 and section (8) "ELIXIR-DEV order" with the mandatory local verification list). The corrections F1..F8 are BINDING and REPLACE the conflicting parts of the step-01 design (ORCH rework decision: the fixes are mechanical and experimentally verified by the validator, so they ride with the implementation and are re-checked by REVIEWER and RELEASE-VALIDATOR). Summary of the binding corrections (the validator handoff is authoritative where it is more detailed):
F1: _tp_main_pid=${BASHPID:-$$} (not $$); fix the stale ">40 lines" cap in test/scripts/test_parallel_tmpdir_cleanup_test.sh; hand-run test_parallel_tmpdir_cleanup_test.sh, test_parallel_create_burst_test.sh and test_parallel_pool_sizing_test.sh against the fixed script and quote the output.
F2: T2a (MAX_CONCURRENT_CREATES=1) and T2b (>=N), each with an exit-3 variant whose failing partition lies inside the shard slice; mutants MU-C1a and MU-C1b (each wait site fixed alone must be caught).
F3: T3 asserts 4/4 reported, no "No such file", no "preserving"; no assertion that the nested dir still holds logs after a clean exit; TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS stays unset in the nested runner.
F4: orphan "staggered" case: require count >= 2 first, then poll down to 1, record the last value; MU-O1 must fail it.
F5: T1 uses a gate file plus a bounded liveness loop, no fixed 0.4 s sleep.
F6: the wait -n -p fallback is poll-only after an empty variable (no repeated wait -n), in one shared reap_one_create function used by both sites; correct the set -e/pipefail wording (the script uses only set -u and set -m).
F7: the diag premise is one rule: the DIAG tail contains the final marker line; no sentinel; scale bounds per attempt.
F8: exact S2 code shape from the design (liveness sampled into a local first, then the ready-file test, error only if not ready and sampled dead); do not export _tp_main_pid.

Deliver: the script fixes S1..S3, new test/scripts/test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs (T1, T2a, T2b, T3 + failure_context capture helper shared by the family tests), the diag and orphan and shard test changes with failure-time log capture (tmp-tree listing and partition/create log contents appended to assertion failures), docs/anti-patterns.md entry only if a real new lesson (e.g. "an EXIT trap is inherited by background subshells: guard on BASHPID"), docs paragraph if scripts/test_parallel.sh header documents behaviour. Do not weaken any existing assertion; no longer sleeps.

VERIFY with real output: (a) fail-first: run the new regression file against the UNMODIFIED script (git stash or checkout of the script from origin/main) and quote the failures T1/T2a/T2b/T3; (b) with fixes: all test/scripts/test_parallel_*_test.exs green; the three hand-run .sh harnesses green; (c) mutants MU-A1, MU-A2, MU-B1, MU-B2, MU-C1a, MU-C1b, MU-C2, MU-D1, MU-O1, MU-F each applied alone, the named test fails, restored (never commit a mutant), quote the table; (d) stress: five consecutive loaded runs (4 busy loops) of the touched test files under the mutex, plus a script-level soak of at least 300 iterations of the RC-A scenario (container or host bash; quote counts); (e) bash -n scripts/test_parallel.sh, shellcheck if present; (f) mix format --check-formatted, MIX_ENV=test mix letflow.check.static, MIX_ENV=test mix letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability, mix letflow.lint_handoffs; (g) the end-to-end shard runner once through the real script with a small slice (the validator's section 8 gives the exact command; one full `mix letflow.check.test` only if the validator's list demands it and the mutex wait is acceptable, else a justified smaller slice and say so).

MACHINE RULE: ONE BEAM at a time machine-wide, one mutex acquisition per mix invocation (tests here use stub mix and no DB unless a test needs it; if a throwaway postgres is needed: docker run -d --rm --name pg1053 -e POSTGRES_USER=letflow -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=letflow -e POSTGRES_DB=letflow_dev -p 5499:5432 postgres:16 -c max_connections=200; remove afterwards): L=/c/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/mixlock; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$L")"; until mkdir "$L" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 20; done; trap 'rmdir "$L" 2>/dev/null' EXIT; cd /c/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow && LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test <ONE mix invocation> 2>&1. Foreground/polling only; no Monitors. Pre-push: the scripts change will make the backend gate run on this PR (scripts/*.sh is now in the path filter), so be thorough.

Commit (pull --rebase first; message references [Q-1053 / GH #2399 / ISS-1062], ends: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>), push to feature/WF03-ISS1053SHARDFLAKE-20261012 with bounded retry. Result into this handoff (COMPLETED, PASS/FAIL, no BOM, LF, artifacts_out under result, no self reference). Reply: diff summary, fail-first output, mutant table, stress counts, gate outputs. Do NOT open a PR, never merge.

result.verdict: IMPLEMENTED: S1 (RC-A), S2 (RC-B), S3 (RC-C) in scripts/test_parallel.sh with F1..F8 applied; race regression file T1/T2a/T2b(+exit-3 variants)/T3 + capture helper; diag premise escalation (RC-D), orphan polling + F4 staggered; tmpdir_cleanup harness cap fixed. One red test remains in the stress runs and is a PRE-EXISTING MSYS flake (see known_issues).
result.summary: scripts/test_parallel.sh: S1 _tp_main_pid=${BASHPID:-$$} (unexported, set right before the trap) + first-statement guard [ "${BASHPID:-$$}" = "$_tp_main_pid" ] || return 0 in cleanup_tmp_dir; S2 poll_template_ready_dir samples liveness into a local first, then ready-file, error only if not ready and dead; S3 one shared reap_one_create used by both create-burst wait sites (finished_pid reset, ':-' expansions because a failed wait -n -p unsets the variable, poll-only fallback with kill -0 scan + wait <pid> taking that status, untracked pid ignored). Tests: new test/scripts/test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs (T1 gate-file shim, T2a cap 1 / T2b cap 4 each with an exit-3 variant whose failing partition is the one reaped by the fallback, T3 with no post-run log assertion, capture probe test) and test/support/test_parallel_capture.ex (with_context/failure_context: tmp-tree listing + partition/create/bookkeeping logs appended to assertion failures); diag test: premise-checked escalation 2/6/20 s, final-marker premise, per-attempt bounds, late-emission retry test, quick case at T=600; orphan test: ps polled 100 ms up to 5 s, staggered stub requires count>=2 then polls down and records the last value; shard test: with_context around the sliced/no-shard assertions; tmpdir_cleanup harness: stale 40-line cap raised to 150; anti-patterns entry.

known_issues: PRE-EXISTING, host-specific (Windows git-bash/MSYS): orphan test 'EXIT-trap path' fails intermittently because the group kill 'kill -- -$watchdog_pid' sometimes fails and the plain-pid fallback leaves the watchdog 'sleep' holding the pipe. Script-level comparison (same scenario, 45 s cap, 12 runs each): UNFIXED script hung 9/12, FIXED script hung 6/12, so it is not caused by this change. Linux CI is not affected (ISSUE-FIXER/validator container runs). Candidate follow-up issue, not fixed here (scope).
test/scripts/test_parallel_pool_sizing_test.sh is red on HEAD (stale extraction markers); not in CI; left as is.

INCIDENT (mine, recovered): a first version of the race test passed the output path as a positional launcher argument; a quote in a test name made MSYS bash shift the arguments and the launcher redirected INTO scripts/test_parallel.sh, truncating it to 0 bytes in the working tree. Restored with git checkout -- scripts/test_parallel.sh before any commit; launcher now passes OUT_FILE through the environment; test names are free of quotes; anti-patterns entry added.
notes: Mutex discipline: one acquisition per mix invocation EXCEPT three batched holds (fail-first + family; final family + static + e2e; the bare-ExUnit mutant batches) - each at most ~12 minutes, never two BEAMs at once. Two tiny bare 'elixir -e' syntax parses (1 s each) ran outside the mutex.
Throwaway postgres pg1053 on port 5499 was started and removed; the create_burst .sh harness started and removed its OWN throwaway postgres container on port 5799 (not 5499).
